## 1. SURFACE
Two-col whitespace/tab table, no header, no units label. Numbers written with comma as decimal mark (`47183,554644`) — EU/German locale style. Col1 monotonic descending (47183 → 1648). Col2 look like intensity counts.

## 2. CONTENT
Col1 = Raman shift, cm⁻¹ (x-axis). Col2 = intensity counts (y-axis). Comma = decimal separator, not thousands-sep, not CSV delimiter — true field separator is tab. Row order descending (high wavenumber → low), not ascending as most fit/plot tools assume by default.
Range (1648–47183 cm⁻¹) way exceeds typical G(~1580)/2D(~2700 cm⁻¹) window shown in sample rows — G/2D peaks sit buried somewhere in unshown middle rows, consistent w/ cm⁻¹ reading, not nm (nm range 200-1100 don't fit values this big).

CONTENT VERDICT: MISMATCH

## 3. MISREADINGS
- **Split on comma as CSV delim** → `47183,554644` parsed as two ints (47183 / 554644) instead of one float 47183.554644. Evidence: comma appears inside every single number, consistent position (6 digits after), classic EU decimal notation not row-delimiter.
- **Comma as thousands-sep (US/UK locale)** → misread as ~47,183,554,646 type garbage value. Evidence: magnitude nonsensical for Raman shift (max real range ~4000-8000 cm⁻¹ even UV instruments); fractional part pattern (6 digits) matches sub-wavenumber resolution, not grouping.
- **Assume ascending x order** (default for many fit libs, e.g. lmfit/scipy peak search) → wrong direction scan or need explicit sort/reverse. Evidence: row1 x=47183 (max), last row x=1648 (min), strictly decreasing throughout sample.
- **Assume col1 is wavelength (nm)** → wrong physical axis, would misplace G/2D peak search. Evidence: values (1648–47183) far outside any real optical wavelength range (200–1100nm); only cm⁻¹ Raman-shift reading puts known G(1580)/2D(2700) peaks inside range.
- **Assume col2 needs unit conversion** (e.g. treat as absorbance/counts/s) — no header confirms, but task context ("output of Raman setup", fit amplitude/offset) implies raw intensity counts; low risk but no explicit label to confirm.
